questions.q: What happens to the underlying semantic model when you share a report?
options: The recipient also gets access to the semantic model, not just the report — hiding elements in the report doesn't restrict this
The semantic model is automatically duplicated and isolated from the original
The semantic model is never accessible to the recipient under any circumstance
Semantic model access must always be granted through a completely separate process
questions.explain: Sharing a report also shares access to its semantic model by default. Hiding a table or column is a clutter-reduction choice, not a security boundary — only RLS or OLS actually restrict data access.

questions.q: Which link type gives NO new access, and is meant only for someone who already has access another way?
options: People with existing access
People in your organization
Specific people
Publish to web
questions.explain: 'People with existing access' generates a URL to the report but grants nothing new — it's for sending a link to someone who can already open the content.

questions.q: What does the 'Build' permission on a shared link allow, that 'Reshare' does not?
options: The recipient can create their own new reports based on the underlying semantic model, in other workspaces
The recipient can only view the report, nothing more
The recipient can delete the original report
The recipient can change the report's title
questions.explain: Reshare lets the recipient pass the link to others. Build is a bigger grant — it lets them create entirely new reports and analysis on top of your semantic model.

questions.q: What is the difference between row-level security (RLS) and object-level security (OLS)?
options: RLS restricts which data rows a user can see; OLS restricts which tables or columns a user can see
RLS and OLS are two names for the exact same feature
OLS only works with DirectQuery, RLS only works with Import
RLS restricts columns; OLS restricts rows
questions.explain: RLS filters rows of data (e.g. a salesperson only sees their region's rows). OLS restricts entire columns or tables from being visible to certain users.

questions.q: Why is 'Publish to web' considered a much bigger risk than the sharing options in this lesson?
options: It makes a report publicly accessible on the internet with no authentication required, including its underlying data
It's functionally identical to sharing with 'People in your organization'
It only shares the report's title, nothing else
It requires every viewer to have a Pro license, making it safer
questions.explain: Publish to web removes authentication entirely — anyone with the link, anywhere, can see the report and its data. It should never be used as a substitute for controlled sharing.
